title: Bitcoin ETF Inflows Hit $3.8B in Three Weeks, 2026's Strongest Run
dek: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $3.8 billion in inflows over a three-week period, the strongest run of 2026, with inflows rising approximately 7 percent week over week. The latest week saw nearly $1 billion in inflows despite Bitcoin briefly dipping below $79,000, while Ether and XRP ETF inflows dropped sharply in the same window.
author: Crypto Cronkite
key_fact: $3.8 billion in three-week Bitcoin ETF inflows marks 2026's strongest consecutive period.
bottom_line: The three-week, $3.8 billion Bitcoin ETF inflow surge reversed earlier 2026 patterns of more balanced institutional allocation between Bitcoin and altcoin products. The divergence will persist if Bitcoin holds above $79,000 and altcoin ETFs continue to see withdrawals; a reversal would signal renewed institutional appetite for Ether or Solana products.
body:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs accumulated $3.8 billion in inflows over a three-week period, according to Cointelegraph, marking the strongest consecutive stretch of 2026. Bitcoin ETF inflows rose approximately 7 percent week over week during the run, with the latest week alone drawing nearly $1 billion.
The momentum persisted even as Bitcoin price volatility remained present: inflows stayed positive on Friday despite Bitcoin briefly falling below $79,000, suggesting institutional demand that extends beyond near-term price action.
The concentrated capital flow into Bitcoin ETFs starkly diverges from the broader crypto market. Ether and XRP ETF inflows dropped sharply during the same three-week window, according to Cointelegraph, a divergence that reflects rotation of institutional capital toward Bitcoin while other crypto products face headwinds.
The latest week's near-$1 billion inflow comes against the backdrop of the desk's ETF flows board showing $174.6 million in Bitcoin spot ETF inflows on September 4 alone, the highest daily figure since January.
Elsewhere, Ethereum spot ETFs drew $25.9 million on September 4 and have accumulated $13.185 billion year-to-date, a substantially slower pace than Bitcoin products.
